overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights that high-concept astronomy, extreme space 'What If' scenarios, and planetary oddities (especially involving rare materials or extreme physics published within the last 7 days) dominate traction. Specifically, videos like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' generated strong view velocity and exceptional engagement relative to their age compared to older evergreen biological or psychological facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Planetary 'What If' / Alternative Physics Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered high views (1024 and 972 respectively) and strong like ratios within days of posting.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' planetary immersion concepts involving extreme environmental hazards (e.g., extreme pressure, weird states of matter).

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-Bending Planetary Extremes with Rare/Precious Materials
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) drove high early-stage engagement and healthy likes-per-view.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form hooks focusing on bizarre astronomical time-dilation, unusual precipitation, or ultra-rare resource anomalies on newly discovered exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5AN7LUgqarc) stalled out significantly lower in views-per-day compared to the space/astronomy cluster.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and earworm micro-facts unless framed through a radically cinematic or high-stakes mystery narrative.

weak_patterns.pattern: Stale Animal Facts Without Extreme Survival Context
weak_patterns.evidence: Basic biology facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) plateaued quickly in daily velocity compared to high-concept space hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal content strictly toward cinematic animal survival, micro-horror/mystery, or extreme adaptations rather than static trivia.

next_video.concept: What If You Stepped Foot on a Rogue Planet Drifting Through the Intergalactic Void?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with total pitch blackness and absolute zero temperature, dropping the viewer directly onto a world with no star.

next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the winning high-velocity 'What If' planet format while introducing a brand-new space phenomenon (rogue planets with subterranean warmth).
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not mention diamonds, liquid metal, glass rain, or burning ice.
Must feature a completely unreleased exoplanet/cosmic object concept.
Strictly factual astrophysical principles applied to speculative immersion.

experiment: Test whether framing an astronomy 'What If' scenario around a rogue planetary core heat source retains viewers longer than surface-level atmospheric oddities like diamond or iron rain.
